title: Ada-KV: Adaptive Budget Allocation for KV Cache Eviction
one_line_claim: Ada-KV is the first head-wise adaptive budget allocation strategy for KV cache eviction that allocates cache budgets proportionally to attention concentration across heads.
method_summary: Ada-KV takes cache budget and per-head attention weight distributions as inputs and allocates cache budgets adaptively to each attention head based on concentration patterns via a safeguard parameter alpha. The output is enhanced cache eviction decisions integrable as a plug-and-play module into existing methods like SnapKV and Pyramid.

key_findings.finding: Provides theoretical L1 upper bound on eviction loss via Theorem 3.1, bounding loss by 2C times the sum of tail attention weights across heads.
key_findings.quote: L1 eviction loss can be bounded by epsilon: L1 Eviction Loss <= epsilon = 2hC - 2C sum(T_i*A_i') where C = Max(||V_i*W_i^T||_infinity)

key_findings.finding: Ada-SnapKV and Ada-Pyramid achieve consistent improvements over baseline SnapKV and Pyramid across 16 datasets on LongBench.
key_findings.quote: the Ada-SnapKV and Ada-Pyramid methods, with our adaptive allocation enhancement, achieve consistent improvements in overall generation quality across different budgets and models.

key_findings.finding: Safeguard parameter alpha=0.2 provides balanced performance across budget levels.
key_findings.quote: Based on this trade-off, we selected a balanced value of alpha = 0.2 in this work.

limitations: Head-wise allocation limited to within a single layer; cross-layer extension future work.
Fixed safeguard parameter rather than per-model fine-tuning may be suboptimal.

relation_to_herald.shared: Both address KV-cache compressed LLM generation by analyzing per-token signals to improve quality and reliability.
differs_on: Ada-KV optimizes cache budget allocation across heads to minimize eviction loss; HERALD predicts catastrophic generation failures from per-token logit features.
Ada-KV is a plug-and-play module for existing eviction methods; HERALD is a separate failure prediction system enabling downstream intervention.
Ada-KV uses attention concentration patterns as its signal; HERALD uses logit distribution statistics and temporal dynamics.
